q: Fluid is a substance that offers no ____ resistance to deforming forces.
e: Fluids yield continuously to deforming forces.

q: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at rest, while fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in ____.
e: Dynamics is the study of fluids in motion.

q: Motion of fluids is an important application in our daily life; such as river flow, water distribution systems, gas pipelines, ____ (travels in air) and motion underneath the surface of water.
e: Aviation relies heavily on fluid dynamics principles.

q: The study of the flow of liquid is called hydrodynamics, whereas hydrostatic is the study of liquid at ____.
e: Hydrostatics deals with liquids at rest.

q: This chapter mainly concerns with hydrodynamics; however a section on surface tension and ____, which are important concepts of hydrostatic, is included at the end of the chapter.
e: Capillarity is a key hydrostatic concept.
Both liquids and gases are classified as fluids.

q: The volume of a gas depends on pressure and temperature obeying Boyle's law and ____ law.
e: Charles' law relates gas volume and temperature.

q: However, the volume of a liquid does not depend on ____ if the temperature is constant.
Hence, the liquid is incompressible (i.e. density of liquid is ____ for any pressure provided that the temperature is kept constant).
In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called ____.
e: A streamline represents the path of fluid particles.

q: Motion of fluids can be classified by two types, laminar flow and ____ flow.
e: Fluid flow is either laminar or turbulent.

q: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers, with each layer moving smoothly past the adjacent layers with no mixing; such a flow is called ____ flow.
e: Laminar flow is smooth and layered.

q: In this steady laminar flow, ____ do not cross each other and every fluid particle arriving at a given point has the same velocity.
e: Streamlines never intersect in laminar flow.

q: If the flow or path of the fluid particles are irregular, their direction is always changing or whirling; this fluid movement is called ____ flow.
e: Turbulent flow is irregular and chaotic.

q: In turbulent flow the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and ____.
e: Turbulence involves rapid changes in speed and direction.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the following facts: The fluid is ____.
e: Ideal fluids are assumed to be incompressible.

q: The flow has no friction or friction is neglected (Internal friction in fluids is called ____ ; and hence, zero viscosity).
The fluid flow is laminar (steady) and ____ flow is not taken into account.
For example, sea breeze is a laminar flow and storm is a ____ flow.
e: Storms exhibit chaotic, turbulent air movement.
